Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

// https://www.lintcode.com/problem/sort-integers-ii/description?_from=ladder&&fromId=1
class Solution {
public:
    /**
     * @param A: an integer array
     * @return: nothing
     */
    void sortIntegers2(vector<int> &A) {
       quickSort(A,0,A.size()-1);
    }
    
    void quickSort(vector<int> &A, int start, int end)
    {
        if(start >= end)
            return;
        int left = start, right = end;
        int pivot = A[start + (end - start) / 2];
       
        while(left <= right){
            while(left <= right && A[left] < pivot) ++ left;
            while(left <= right && A[right] > pivot) --right;
            if(left <= right) swap(A[left++],A[right--]);
        }
        quickSort(A,start,right);
        quickSort(A,left,end);
    }
};
